column1: TABLE RoommateStatus-main-comment-likes-v2 - likes on activity and request comments. One row per user per liked comment: a like is a single conditional put keyed by a deterministic id, an unlike is a delete. No itemType — each row self-describes its parent (activity likes set activityId, request likes set requestId). Every row carries a groupId so feeds stay isolated per household. Written by activities.py (id "comment-like#<activityId>#<commentId>#<userId>") and household_requests.py (id "request-comment-like#<requestId>#<commentId>#<userId>"). Keyed (groupId HASH, id RANGE): the group is the partition, so reading a household's feed is one Query and no row can be addressed from another household. The -v2 suffix is historical: this replaced an id-keyed table of the same name, which a key-schema change could not alter in place.
